subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows PowerShell expansion-bearing exec commands be allowed only through explicit one-shot approval, as proposed in #100322, or should OpenClaw keep rejecting/documenting them as unsupported?
rationale: Current source rejects the reported syntax, while passing it through touches exec approval semantics and needs a deliberate security/product contract for command fidelity on Windows.

options.title: Land one-shot explicit approval
options.body: Proceed with #100322 or a successor once real Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion tokens are reviewed and executed only through one-shot approval.

options.title: Keep rejecting and document
options.body: Treat PowerShell expansion-bearing commands as unsupported in approval-managed Windows exec and document script-file or environment workarounds.

options.title: Design broader Windows shell contract
options.body: Pause the issue for a fuller Windows exec command-fidelity design that covers PowerShell, cmd wrappers, approval rendering, and docs together.

recommendation.title: Land one-shot explicit approval
recommendation.body: Proceed with #100322 or a successor once real Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion tokens are reviewed and executed only through one-shot approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current behavior appears to live in the command planner/authorization surface associated with this history.
